articles.title: 11 artists look beyond the Himalayan landscape at Takpa Gallery
articles.summary: The Takpa Gallery in Kathmandu is hosting ‘Voices from the Himalayas’, an exhibition featuring eleven artists who explore life beyond the iconic mountain scenery. The show highlights the region’s diverse peoples, cultures and the social and environmental changes affecting them, offering viewers a nuanced perspective of the Himalayas as a lived space rather than just a landscape.

articles.title: Mental wellbeing: There’s more to ‘feeling better’ after a walk in nature than you might think
articles.summary: The article explores how spending time in natural environments can boost mental wellbeing beyond simple relaxation. It explains that trees emit chemicals like phytoncides that may improve immune function and mood, while green spaces provide a restorative break for the brain, reducing stress and enhancing cognitive performance. The piece cites research linking regular walks in nature to lower anxiety and depression rates, and suggests incorporating green areas into daily routines for lasting psychological benefits.

articles.title: Iran vows to retaliate after US widens sanctions
articles.summary: Iran has pledged to retaliate against the United States after Washington broadened its sanctions regime, warning that it could target U.S. interests and critical energy chokepoints worldwide. Beijing has dismissed the sanctions as pressure tactics, emphasizing its opposition to external interference. The heightened rhetoric has sent oil markets into a cautious stance, with traders anticipating possible supply disruptions. The development underscores rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the broader impact on global energy security.

articles.title: Court orders government to ensure dairy farmers are paid on time
articles.summary: The Nepalese Supreme Court has ordered the government to guarantee that dairy farmers receive their payments on schedule. The court warned that contractual agreements should not be used to silence farmers who lack direct access to authorities, emphasizing the need for transparent and timely financial processes in the agricultural sector.

articles.title: Jimmy Neesham returns to Janakpur Bolts for NPL third season
articles.summary: New Zealand all‑rounder Jimmy Neesham has re‑joined the Janakpur Bolts ahead of the third season of Nepal's National Premier League (NPL). Neesham was instrumental in Janakpur's triumph in the inaugural 2024 NPL, helping the team secure the title. His return is expected to boost the Bolts' chances of defending their championship and adds excitement for fans as the league prepares for its upcoming season.

articles.title: Nepal’s parliament debates capital punishment following rape and murder of a three-year-old
articles.summary: The Nepalese parliament is debating the reinstatement of capital punishment after a high‑profile case in Jeetpur‑Simara where a three‑year‑old girl was raped and murdered. The brutal crime has sparked nationwide outrage, prompting the law and home ministers to present proposed legal reforms while explaining why the death penalty remains legally unattainable under the current constitution. The discussion highlights tensions between public demand for harsher penalties and constitutional constraints, with lawmakers weighing possible amendments to the criminal code.

articles.title: Trump administration plans to revoke visas of foreigners seeking asylum
articles.summary: The Trump administration announced a plan to revoke the visas of up to 200,000 foreign nationals who hold business or tourism visas and have applied for asylum in the United States. The policy is part of a broader crackdown on immigration, aiming to deter asylum seekers and tighten visa enforcement. Critics argue the move could harm legitimate travelers and businesses, while supporters claim it will protect national security and reduce fraudulent claims.

articles.title: Prime Minister Balendra Shah gets a medical pass for dark shades as Parliament bans them
articles.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah has been granted a medical exemption to wear dark sunglasses after doctors advised that he needs eye protection from bright light. Meanwhile, Parliament has issued a rule prohibiting lawmakers from wearing dark glasses inside the House, creating a contrast between the PM’s allowance and the legislative ban.

articles.title: Lawmakers demand action over rape and killing of three-year-old in Bara
articles.summary: Lawmakers in Nepal's National Assembly have called for urgent government action after a three‑year‑old girl was raped and murdered in Bara district. The incident has sparked outrage over rising insecurity and violence against girls, with legislators accusing the government of failing to protect citizens. They also alleged that the victim's family faced pressure while a video of the crime was being filmed. The assembly members demanded stronger law enforcement, faster judicial processes, and support for the family, highlighting broader concerns about public safety and gender‑based violence in the country.

articles.title: NADA Auto Show 2026 opens in Kathmandu
articles.summary: The NADA Auto Show 2026 has opened in Kathmandu for a six‑day exhibition. Over 150 automotive brands and more than 200 stalls are presenting new vehicles, auto components and financial services. Organisers emphasize the event’s role in promoting the automotive sector’s contribution to job creation and economic growth in Nepal.

articles.title: 24 years after leaving Nepal, he came home blind and broken
articles.summary: Hom Bahadur Gharti left Nepal for Malaysia in 2002 seeking work. Over the years he lived illegally, lost contact with his family, and endured harsh conditions. After two decades abroad, he was discovered in a severely deteriorated state—blind and physically broken—and was repatriated to Nepal this year. The story highlights the plight of Nepali migrant workers, the risks of undocumented labor abroad, and the personal tragedy of a man who spent his prime years far from home, returning home in a tragic condition.

articles.title: Two die as scrub typhus spreads in Salyan
articles.summary: A scrub typhus outbreak in Salyan district has claimed two lives, with four to five new cases confirmed daily in the Darma area. The rapid spread is exacerbated by a shortage of testing kits, forcing patients to travel to other districts for diagnosis and treatment. Health officials warn that the lack of resources could lead to a wider epidemic if not addressed promptly.

articles.title: Bangladesh could consider joining Mecca pact, in test for foreign ties
articles.summary: Bangladesh is weighing the possibility of joining the Mecca pact, a collective‑defence agreement recently signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan in Mecca. The pact mirrors NATO’s principle of mutual defense among the three Sunni‑majority nations, and Bangladesh’s potential participation could signal a shift in its foreign policy toward deeper ties with these countries.

articles.title: Nepal crush Malaysia in ACC Premier Cup warm-up
articles.summary: In a warm‑up match for the ACC Premier Cup, Nepal defeated Malaysia by crushing the rain‑adjusted target of 228 runs in just 28 overs. Aasif Sheikh anchored the innings with a blistering 161, while opening partner Arjun Kumal contributed to a 220‑run opening partnership, ensuring a dominant chase.

articles.title: We’re changing how Kantipur is funded. Here’s what it means for you.
articles.summary: Kantipur Media Group announced two major changes to its funding model to improve financial sustainability and transparency. The first change involves introducing a subscription-based revenue stream, encouraging readers to support quality journalism directly. The second focuses on diversifying advertising sources and exploring new digital monetisation methods. The announcement explains how these shifts will affect readers, advertisers, and the broader media landscape in Nepal, promising more reliable content while maintaining affordable access.

articles.title: DDC moves to put Dolpa’s yak cheese on the market
articles.summary: The District Development Committee (DDC) is launching a new dairy plant in Jagadulla, Dolpa, capable of producing up to 30 tonnes of yak cheese annually. The initiative aims to provide a guaranteed market for yak and chauri products, encouraging farmers to revive commercial yak and chauri farming throughout the district. Stakeholders see the plant as a catalyst for local economic growth and preservation of traditional livestock practices.

articles.title: Kiran Thapa Magar wins confidence vote in Bagmati
articles.summary: Chief Minister Kiran Thapa Magar secured a confidence vote in Bagmati Province, receiving 57 of the 58 votes cast in the provincial assembly. The session was attended by 58 lawmakers, while opposition parties stayed away, effectively boycotting the vote.

articles.title: Nepal, US plan high-level visits and other engagements next year
articles.summary: Nepal and the United States have announced plans for a series of high‑level visits and cooperative engagements in the coming year. After eight decades of diplomatic ties, both countries aim to deepen their partnership across three strategic pillars: accelerating Nepal's digital transformation, expanding clean energy collaboration, and investing in human capital development. The initiatives are expected to involve senior officials from both governments and could include trade delegations, technology exchanges, and joint projects to support Nepal's economic growth and sustainability goals.

articles.title: Sugar stocks were said to be sufficient. Prices are now surging
articles.summary: Nepal's sugar reserves, previously deemed sufficient for six months, are now under strain as prices climb sharply ahead of the upcoming festive season. The surge in sugar costs is causing concern among consumers and traders, prompting warnings about potential shortages and the impact on household budgets.

articles.title: Indoor mould is a public health issue requiring attention
articles.summary: A recent article highlights indoor mould as an emerging public health concern in Nepal. Prolonged exposure to mould spores can gradually poison indoor air and accumulate in the body, leading to respiratory problems, allergies, and other chronic illnesses. The piece calls for increased awareness, better ventilation standards, regular inspections, and coordinated action by health authorities and housing agencies to mitigate the risk. It stresses that addressing indoor mould requires both public education and policy interventions to protect citizens’ long‑term health.

articles.title: Towards a Pax Sinica in South Asia?
articles.summary: The article examines India's growing willingness to normalise ties with China as the United States' global dominance wanes. It argues that New Delhi recognizes the need to adapt to a new geopolitical reality, where a potential "Pax Sinica" could shape South Asian affairs. The piece discusses the strategic uncertainties facing India, the shifting balance of power, and the implications of deeper Indo‑Chinese engagement for regional stability and India's own foreign policy autonomy.

articles.title: Essential vaccines are running out in Nepal. It’s time to act
articles.summary: Nepal is facing critical shortages of essential vaccines and acute therapies as the country enters peak disease seasons, prompting urgent calls for government and international action to secure supplies and prevent outbreaks.

articles.title: How Abiral Pratap Adhikary finds comfort and perspective online
articles.summary: Kathmandu-based actor Abiral Pratap Adhikary shares how he finds comfort and perspective through his online watchlist, highlighting the videos, podcasts, and creators that influence him. The piece explores his personal media habits, offering insight into the digital content that shapes his outlook and creative process.

articles.title: Movie review: ‘Masterni’ answers the mystery but forgets the suspense
articles.summary: The review of the Nepali film 'Masterni' praises its intriguing premise and unconventional storytelling, but criticizes its heavy reliance on exposition which hampers the buildup of genuine suspense. While the narrative ambition is noted, the execution falls short in maintaining tension, leaving the audience with a resolved mystery but a lackluster experience.

articles.title: China, India hold border talks, agree to continue search for boundary settlement
articles.summary: China and India have resumed border talks, reaffirming their commitment to a peaceful resolution of their long‑standing boundary dispute. The discussions come after the deadly 2020 clash and a four‑year military standoff, with both sides agreeing to keep diplomatic channels open and to hold the next round of negotiations in India in 2027. The talks signal a mutual desire to stabilise bilateral ties and avoid further escalation along the contested frontier.
